newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - July 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - July 3.

text.p: Following are the highlights of Irish press on Thursday:
- A 500 million Irish pound cash boost to the Exchequer leaves Finance Minister Charlie McCreevy poised for a major tax-cutting budget in November.
- Former Prime Minister Charles J. Haughey was the sole political figure to benefit from the so-called Ansbacher Deposits that held up to 40 million Irish pounds, top level sources said last night.

- A death threat to civilians in the Irish republic from a small but ruthless loyalist group has added an extra dimension to anxiety over the North, already gripped by fears that widespread order could follow Sunday's Drumcree march.
- A payments to politician tribunal will make a public statement, possibly today, explaining its reluctance to heed opposition calls to widen its terms of reference.
- Next Sunday's planned Orange Order parade at Drumcree will top the agenda at the first meeting between Irish Prime Minister Bertie Ahern and Britain's Tony Blair on Thursday.
- Strong growth in tax receipts indicates that government borrowing will probably be eliminated completely this year and that the economy is growing much more rapidly than expected.
- Prime Ministers Tony Blair and Bertie Ahern will hold talks on Thursday on the marching season despite a cross-border strike threat by loyalist terrorists.

- Education minister Michael Martin last night confirmed he had appointed an inspector to conduct two inquiries into a case whre a school principal has been suspended following allegations of impersonation during exams.

- The payments-to-politicians inquiry is expected to issue a public statement shortly that no other politicians other than Charles J. Haughey have been paid out of a secret 40 million pound bank account once run by the former Prime Minister's top accountant.
